kings2.17.p1.b1.text: In the twelfth year of the reign of Ahaz over Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria nine years. And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, but not like the kings of Israel who preceded him.

kings2.17.p1.b2.text: Shalmaneser king of Assyria attacked him, and Hoshea became his vassal and paid him tribute.

kings2.17.p1.b3.text: … Hoshea had conspired to send envoys to King So of Egypt, and … he had not paid tribute to the king of Assyria as in previous years.

kings2.17.p1.b4.text: … the king of Assyria arrested Hoshea and put him in prison.

kings2.17.p2.b1.text: Then the king of Assyria invaded the whole land, marched up to Samaria, and besieged it for three years.

kings2.17.p2.b2.text: In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria and carried away the Israelites to Assyria, where he settled them in Halah, in Gozan by the Habor River, and in the cities of the Medes.

kings2.17.p3.b1.text: All this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the LORD their God, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt. They had worshiped other gods

kings2.17.p3.b2.text: The Israelites secretly did things against the LORD their God that were not right. From watchtower to fortified city, they built high places in all their cities.

kings2.17.p3.b3.text: They set up for themselves sacred pillars and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.

kings2.17.p3.b4.text: They served idols, although the LORD had told them, “You shall not do this thing.”

kings2.17.p4.b1.text: Yet through all His prophets and seers, the LORD warned Israel and Judah, saying, “Turn from your wicked ways and keep My commandments and statutes …”

kings2.17.p4.b2.text: But they would not listen, and they stiffened their necks like their fathers, who did not believe the LORD their God.

kings2.17.p4.b3.text: … made for themselves two cast idols of calves and an Asherah pole. They bowed down to all the host of heaven and served Baal.

kings2.17.p4.b4.text: They sacrificed their sons and daughters in the fire and practiced divination and soothsaying. They devoted themselves to doing evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger.

kings2.17.p5.b1.text: So the LORD was very angry with Israel, and He removed them from His presence. Only the tribe of Judah remained,

kings2.17.p5.b2.text: and even Judah did not keep the commandments of the LORD their God, but lived according to the customs Israel had introduced.

kings2.17.p5.b3.text: … Jeroboam led Israel away from following the LORD and caused them to commit a great sin.

kings2.17.p5.b4.text: … So Israel was exiled from their homeland into Assyria, where they are to this day.

kings2.17.p6.b1.text: Then the king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim and settled them in the towns of Samaria to replace the Israelites. …

kings2.17.p6.b2.text: Now when the settlers first lived there, they did not worship the LORD, so He sent lions among them, which killed some of them.

kings2.17.p6.b3.text: “The peoples that you have removed and placed in the cities of Samaria do not know the requirements of the God of the land. …”

kings2.17.p6.b4.text: Thus one of the priests they had carried away came and lived in Bethel, and he began to teach them how they should worship the LORD.

kings2.17.p7.b1.text: Nevertheless, the people of each nation continued to make their own gods in the cities where they had settled, and they set them up in the shrines that the people of Samaria had made on the high places.

kings2.17.p7.b2.text: The men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, the men of Cuth made Nergal, the men of Hamath made Ashima, the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak, …

kings2.17.p7.b3.text: So the new residents worshiped the LORD, but they also appointed for themselves priests of all sorts to serve in the shrines of the high places.

kings2.17.p7.b4.text: They worshiped the LORD, but they also served their own gods according to the customs of the nations from which they had been carried away.

kings2.17.p8.b1.text: To this day they are still practicing their former customs. None of them worship the LORD or observe the statutes, ordinances, laws, and commandments that the LORD gave the descendants of Jacob, …

kings2.17.p8.b2.text: “Do not worship other gods or bow down to them; do not serve them or sacrifice to them. … worship the LORD your God, and He will deliver you from the hands of all your enemies.”

kings2.17.p8.b3.text: But they would not listen, and they persisted in their former customs.

kings2.17.p8.b4.text: So these nations worshiped the LORD but also served their idols, and to this day their children and grandchildren continue to do as their fathers did.
